solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lacking funds after holiday? Support needed

indicators.note: after places the funds piece behind the holiday piece in the answer

parts.note: a trip is a holiday or excursion
OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn, short of money

explanation.surface: Someone broke after a holiday needs financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' reads as financial help, but it is a three-legged stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged stand holding up a camera is a kind of support.

clue.text: Spreads out as a tired drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A weary drunk sprawling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that radiates spreads outward from a centre, like light or heat.

clue.text: Globe-trotting Michael loses heart, suffering?

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letter of the surname is dropped

parts.note: Michael Palin, the British comedian known for round-the-world travel programmes

explanation.surface: A weary travelling celebrity losing his enthusiasm and hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Palin is a Monty Python member who presented TV travel series such as Around the World in 80 Days.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is suffering, physical or mental distress.

clue.text: Prepare to tackle The Listener at home? This may produce tedium

indicators.note: to tackle means the prepare word takes hold of the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to dress is to prepare, as with food or a wound
the ear is the organ that listens
in means at home

explanation.surface: Getting ready to do the Listener crossword at home, which may be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard crossword in The Times, but here it is simply an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreariness is dull gloom, a synonym for tedium or boredom.

clue.text: Bird, one quietly occupying hole in the ground

indicators.note: occupying means the one-and-quietly letters sit inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole dug in the ground
I is the Roman numeral one
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A bird nesting quietly in a hollow in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadow pipit is a small brown songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Inn with post office woman's set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the woman's word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ada's, the possessive of the woman's name Ada

explanation.surface: A woman's inn that also houses the local post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is a Spanish or Latin American inn, a crossword-friendly loanword.

clue.text: Leader of party — therefore male when discharged to become this maybe?

definitions.text: Leader of party — therefore male when discharged to become this maybe?

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word party
discharged as in let off or fired, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A male party leader, once dismissed, may be sent to the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when discharged' rearranges THEREFORE MALE behind the P. As a whole, the clue describes a sacked party leader being given a peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is a member of the British nobility sitting in the House of Lords, a common reward for retired party leaders.

clue.text: A duty's becoming tricky around end of the 24-hour period

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the final letter
becoming tricky suggests the letters are twisted into a new arrangement

parts.note: duty's with its s counted as a letter

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A task turning awkward late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming tricky' rearranges A DUTY'S into TUSDAY, which goes 'around' E, the end of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuesday is a day of the week, an example of a 24-hour period.

clue.text: Trips made by Europeans across frontier of continent

indicators.note: across means the Europeans word spans the frontier letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark, Europeans

indicators.note: frontier of takes the first letter of the word continent

explanation.surface: Journeys made by Europeans across a continental border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' looks like journeys, but it is light steps: to trip is to dance nimbly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to step lightly, as in tripping the light fantastic, so dances is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tiresome lot, so annoying ultimately when it's stormy?

definitions.text: Tiresome lot, so annoying ultimately when it's stormy?

indicators.note: stormy suggests the letters are tossed about into a new order
ultimately takes the final letter of the word annoying

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters as a tedious bunch who grate most when storms arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Anagram TIRESOME LOT SO plus G (end of 'annoying'). As a whole, the clue grumbles about forecasters, who dominate the news in storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists study and forecast the weather, so they are the people heard most when it is stormy.

clue.text: What won't help you remember something resembling a riddle

definitions.meaning: a forgetful mind that retains nothing
a riddle is a coarse sieve, so this is a thing that looks like one

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like thing that is no aid to memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but here it is a garden sieve for soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a memory that lets everything fall through, so it is no help to recall; literally it is a skull full of holes like a sieve.

clue.text: Contemporary new design for alcove

indicators.note: a new design of the word alcove means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A modern makeover for a recess in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contemporary' looks like a style of decor, but it is the noun: someone of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: A coeval is a person living at the same time, which is a contemporary.

clue.text: Nasty car crossing river in northern city

indicators.note: crossing means the nasty word spans the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: nasty means bad
R is the map abbreviation for river
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: An unpleasant car fording a river near a city in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a large city in West Yorkshire in the north of England.

clue.text: Feat of a person abstaining isn't grabbing chaps

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a person who abstains from alcohol

indicators.note: grabbing means the isn't word holds the chaps word inside it

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial isn't
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A teetotaller's achievement in not grabbing men.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is an accomplishment or achievement, so a feat.

clue.text: Three (not two or four!) pennies cast into lake

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters are shuffled
the second and fourth letters of the word three are dropped

explanation.surface: Three coins tossed into a lake, perhaps for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not two or four' removes the 2nd and 4th letters (H, E) from THREE, leaving TRE; 'cast' rearranges TRE with PENNIES. The Serpentine is the lake in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serpentine is a well-known lake in Hyde Park, London, so it is an example of a lake.

clue.text: Don't go melodramatic — it's no good

indicators.note: no here means without, so the good letter is taken away

parts.note: stagy means theatrical, melodramatic

explanation.surface: A plea not to leave because the theatrics are pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain, the opposite of going; the imperative matches the clue's command.

clue.text: Like old-fashioned punishment for soldier?

definitions.meaning: of the body, as in physical beating, now outdated in schools
a non-commissioned army rank above lance ...

explanation.surface: Asking whether a soldier deserves an old-style beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal punishment is physical punishment; a corporal is also a junior army officer rank.

clue.text: Works with little time to lose to produce paintings

indicators.note: to lose means the time letter is dropped from the works word

parts.note: toils means works hard
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An artist working against the clock to turn out pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils are pictures done in oil paint, so the word stands for paintings.

clue.text: Flap's at an end with chum turning up

parts.note: over means finished, at an end

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the chum word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pal is a chum

explanation.surface: A panic is over now that a friend has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like a panic, but it is a fold of material that lies over another.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is a part that extends over another, like a flap on an envelope.

clue.text: Stars of intelligence agency catching fool that is given outside work

indicators.note: catching means the agency letters close around everything else

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the that-is letters are placed outside the work letters

parts.note: IE is id est, Latin for that is
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Spies nabbing an idiot who has been sent out on a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassiopeia is a constellation, a group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Reluctant to use old Bible language

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible of 1611
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to use archaic biblical wording.
explanation.definitionFit: To be averse is to be opposed or disinclined, so reluctant.

clue.text: Neglect has upset US soldier — no English soldiers to provide support

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the soldier word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An American soldier is unhappy that no British troops will back him up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it, so neglect is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Attractive figure ultimately no good — getting older

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word figure

parts.note: aging means getting older

explanation.surface: A once attractive figure going downhill with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engaging charms and draws you in, so it is attractive.

clue.text: Territory — it's almost spring in this place

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the spring word is cut off

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A remark that spring has nearly arrived in a particular region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source, SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere of influence is an area of control, so sphere can mean territory or domain.

clue.text: Blame nobody for having the last word

indicators.note: having means the two words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Don't blame anyone for insisting on the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' looks like having the final say in an argument, but it is the word ending a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer or hymn, literally its final word.

clue.text: Mislay personal things in playground game and go mad

definitions.text: Mislay personal things in playground game
definitions.meaning: literally, to misplace your own glass balls in a children's game
to become crazy, lose your reason

explanation.surface: A child loses their marbles in the playground and throws a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose your sanity, as though your wits were small balls that rolled away.

clue.text: Law-enforcers dispossessed to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the word dispossessed is used

explanation.surface: Police who have been partly stripped of their property.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Prickly feeling means he must leave the fireside

indicators.note: must leave means the two letters of he are taken out

parts.note: an ingle is a fireplace or chimney corner

explanation.surface: A man sent away from the warm hearth, getting goosebumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from THE INGLE to leave T plus INGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tingle is a stinging or prickling sensation in the skin.
